name: Strass im Zillertal
kurzbeschreibung: Village at the northern entrance to the Zillertal, where the Ziller flows into the Inn – the gateway to the valley.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Strass im Zillertal is situated at an elevation of 523 meters in the Tyrolean Unterinntal, right at the confluence of the river Ziller and the river Inn. With around 850 residents, the charming village is traditionally known as the scenic gateway to the Zillertal. The village silhouette is strikingly dominated by the steep, forested rock face of Brettfall, rising directly behind the houses. Strass combines the open plains of the Inntal with the alpine grandeur of the Zillertal, serving outdoor travelers as an ideal base for cycling, hiking, and exploring the surrounding mountain ranges.

Geschichte

The settlement history of Strass reaches back into the High Middle Ages. In 1120, the village was first recorded in historical documents as Straze, a Middle High German name referring to its vital position along the ancient crossroads between the Inntal and Zillertal travel routes. The historic district of Rotholz was mentioned in 1180 under the nobles of Rottenburg. Between 1575 and 1585, Archduke Ferdinand II transformed Schloss Rotholz into a Renaissance residence, which today houses the renowned Tyrolean Agricultural College and dairy. Perched on a cliff high above the village stands the pilgrimage church of Maria Brettfall, first noted in the Schwaz mining register of 1536. Originally founded by miners and hermits, the current Baroque church was consecrated in 1729. When Emperor Joseph II banned pilgrimages in 1786, the hermit Franz Margreiter traveled to Vienna to successfully plead for its reinstatement. The late Gothic village church dedicated to St. Jakobus der Ältere was constructed around 1500 and features magnificent Baroque ceiling frescoes created by Anton Kirchebner in 1747.

Anreise

Strass im Zillertal enjoys excellent transport connectivity. Drivers take the Inntalautobahn A12 to the Wiesing/Zillertal/Achensee exit and continue along the B169 Zillertalstraße directly into the village. Rail travelers benefit from the nearby railway hub of Jenbach, served by ÖBB Railjets, Westbahn, and ICE trains. From Jenbach, the scenic narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn reaches Strass im Zillertal in just four minutes. Regular VVT bus line 8330 runs every half hour. Cyclists can access the town easily, as both the Innradweg R3 and the Zillertal-Radweg intersect directly in Strass.

Tipps

A premier highlight is the scenic walk up to Maria Brettfall. A forested Stations of the Cross trail leads in about 40 minutes to the rocky vantage point, rewarded by panoramic views across the Inntal, the Rofan mountains, and the lower Zillertal. Cycling enthusiasts can set off on the flat, family-friendly Zillertal-Radweg following the turquoise river to Mayrhofen, or pedal along the Innradweg to the medieval glassmaking town of Rattenberg. A stroll through Rotholz offers the chance to sample award-winning Tyrolean alpine cheeses at the agricultural college's specialty farm shop.
